facts.text: BuildIndexFiles orders each node's children by Names.Normalize of the segment and then by the segment, both ordinal.
A node's Conflicts and Gaps are the sum over its own subjects plus its children's totals, computed in the local Finish walk.
A group slug that is already taken is retried with a -2, -3 suffix until the slug is unique.
Put records a warning that an index file over --index-max-tokens cannot be split further.
BucketLeaves packs leaf children into synthetic folders named part-1, part-2 and so on, one index file per part.
BucketLeaves returns without doing anything when the node has no leaf children.
Emit writes the full render when it fits the cap and otherwise emits non-leaf children first, then writes a flat render.
RenderRoot re-renders the root at most 6 times so the largest-index token figure it states is stable.
The root index opens with the heading Index, while any other index file is titled Index: followed by its path.
Every index file writes one table whose columns are subject, kind, facts, conflicts, gaps, tokens and file.
at: b.Append("| subject | kind | facts | conflicts | gaps | tokens | file |\n");

facts.text: A row's tokens cell is the chars/4, rounded-up estimate of the cost of reading that row's file.
A group row links to the child's FilePath at the root and to the child slug plus .md inside a sub-index.
Only the root index ends with a Totals section listing subjects, facts, conflicts, gaps, subject-file tokens and the count and largest size of index files.
A non-root index ends with an Up link to its parent file, or to ../INDEX.md when the parent is the root.
at: var upTarget = up.Parent is null ? "../INDEX.md" : up.FileSlug + ".md";

facts.text: The root Totals subject-file token line is fed from subjectTokens summed over every subject, not the row estimates.
The no-conflicts fallback in the root index says None and links to conflicts.md instead of listing subjects.
A group index file is flat, so its own subject rows and its leaf children's rows are all written without indentation.
at: // A group file is flat: every row is an immediate child, so none is indented.

facts.text: When a child would push a part over the cap, BucketLeaves removes it from that part and starts a fresh part with it.
at: // This child pushes the file over the cap: start a new part with it.

facts.text: In shard mode RenderAgentsFile says the bundle was published in shard mode and has no subjects directories, fact files or asset files.
at: This bundle was published in shard mode (`--respect-limits`).

facts.text: The non-shard AGENTS.md gives the drill-down path as AGENTS.md, INDEX.md, index groups, subjects slug index.md, then a fact file.
RenderAgentsFile always points the reader to INDEX.md as the starting file.
The README says the timestamp is kept as-is while the content is unchanged, so republishing identical inputs rewrites nothing.

facts.text: The README budget line describes complete mode as the highlight threshold with every fact listed and strict mode as a hard cutoff.
An asset file name uses the first 8 hex characters of sha256 and a slugified stem of at most 40 characters.
at: the first 8 hex characters of the blob's sha256

facts.text: A subject directory name is at most 80 characters and becomes subject when lowercasing and trimming leave nothing.
at: at most 80 characters; `subject` if nothing is left

facts.text: When a scope name is given the README describes it as that subject and its descendants.
The manifest root object carries a format field set to 1.
The manifest options object records assets, budget, budget_mode, depth, facts, index_max_tokens, subject and subject_id.
A missing asset records only missing true and sha256, with no bytes or mime keys.
A subject's pin is written only when the pin is an object holding both a string repo and a string rev.

facts.text: In shard mode a subject path is shards followed by its shard number and the subject slug as an anchor.
A subject entry gains a parent key only when the parent id is non-null and has a slug in the map.
The manifest file list appends BundleManifest to the generated files, removes duplicates and sorts ordinal.
When a profile is present the options object gains profile as its name and respect_limits as whether a shard set exists.
The shards map is keyed shards/<n>.md starting at 1 and holds each shard's byte count and subject slugs.
BuildManifest returns the JSON text with one trailing newline appended.
Each index path in the manifest is mapped to its token estimate from the tokens dictionary.
Each manifest fact entry holds its id, its path and the slug of its subject.
Each shard entry's bytes value is the UTF-8 byte count of that shard's text.
WriteSorted writes object keys ordered by ordinal string comparison, which makes the manifest output stable.

facts.text: WriteSorted throws InvalidOperationException naming an unsupported manifest value for any other type.
HashFiles feeds each path, its content length and its content, each followed by a NUL byte, into the hash.
Each asset contributes the literal asset, its path, its sha and either missing or present to the hash input.
The bundle hash is the SHA256 digest rendered as lowercase hex.
ReadPreviousManifest returns null when manifest.json does not exist in the output directory.
ReadPreviousManifest returns null when the previous manifest fails to parse as JSON.
ReadPreviousManifest returns the bundle_hash string and every string entry of the files array.

facts.text: ReadPreviousTimestamp reads README.md and extracts the Generated at value with a multiline anchored regex.
at: var match = Regex.Match(File.ReadAllText(path, Utf8NoBom), @"^- Generated at: `(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\dZ)`$", RegexOptions.Multiline);

facts.text: ReadPreviousTimestamp returns null when README.md is absent from the output directory.
SynthesizeCommandLine always includes budget, budget-mode, depth, facts, assets and index-max-tokens after the out path.
The respect-limits flag is appended last, and only when the options set it.
The synthesized command line puts the subject flag and its value before the budget options.
IsBundlePath rejects an empty path, any path containing two dots or a backslash, and any path starting with a slash.
At depth one IsBundlePath accepts the five top-level markdown names, the manifest name, or a JSONL data file.
At depth two IsBundlePath accepts subjects, facts, index or shards followed by an md name longer than three characters, or a JSONL asset path.
at: 2 => parts[0] is "subjects" or "facts" or "index" or "shards" && parts[1].EndsWith(".md", StringComparison.Ordinal) && parts[1].Length > 3

facts.text: At depth four IsBundlePath accepts a fact path or an asset path matched by the compiled regexes.
At depth three IsBundlePath accepts a legacy asset path or a subject index path.
WriteTextIfChanged returns 0 and writes nothing when the existing file already holds the same text.
WriteTextIfChanged returns 1 after writing the file with UTF-8 without a BOM.
WriteTextIfChanged creates the file's parent directory before comparing or writing.
WriteBundle throws a DossierRequestException with code publish_conflict before writing anything when a generated path holds a file the bundle never produced.
The manifest path is exempt from the foreign-file check, so a hand-edited manifest.json is allowed to be replaced.
The publish_conflict message lists the clashing paths and advises moving them or choosing another out directory.
Binary JSONL files are compared and written as bytes and never through a text decode.
at: // Binary files (JSONL data) are compared and written as bytes, never through a text decode.

PublishResult files are the text, binary and asset keys combined and sorted ordinal.
An asset file is re-copied only when it is absent or its bytes differ from the blob.
WriteBundle filters the previous manifest's file list through IsBundlePath before pruning.
